editorial.headline: The Business of Selling Physical Video Games in Indonesia
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this physical-games retail activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration anywhere in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering KBLI 47402, the essential conclusion is geographical: it cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today. That is despite a national classification of TERBUKA and a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The Bali result is not a reduced ownership allowance. It is a registration block, applied under the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium for PMA activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. The record states that, at the Besar scale, every scope of this activity carries a Low or Medium-Low OSS risk assessment; Bali therefore marks it BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO.

At its centre, this is a retail trade activity for video-game console equipment and for video-game products sold in physical form. The record is specific about the tangible formats: cartridges, CDs, DVDs, and other physical forms. That focus gives the classification its practical shape: the retail sale of equipment and physical game products. Direct sales are also noted in the recorded scope.

The classification is available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record therefore opens the activity across the full stated range of scales. Yet it also provides the decisive Bali-specific detail for a foreign-owned registration: the risk finding cited for the Besar scale connects this activity to the province-wide PMA moratorium. National scale availability should be read alongside, rather than in place of, the Bali registration position.

Nationally, the position is straightforward: PMA is open, with ownership permitted up to 100%, under the cited Perpres sources. In Bali, the conclusion is equally straightforward but different: a PMA investor cannot register this activity on the island today, because the relevant Low and Medium-Low risk categories are blocked permanently. These are two distinct layers of the same record—national access on one hand, and a Bali-specific registration prohibition on the other—without turning the national 100% ceiling into a Bali permission.
